records.note: 'Private Equity will see the goldmine in Accelerated TMS ... for dogs' names no firm, target, transaction, countable set, series or date, and 'see the goldmine' is not an observable event. The veterinary twist is joke framing, but the primary failure is that no company_event or quantity_threshold can be written without inventing an acquirer or a metric. Same reading as the earlier private-equity class claims.

event.asset: Accelerated TMS protocols for depression (more than one TMS session per day, including accelerated iTBS and fMRI-guided SAINT-type protocols)
event.title: UnitedHealthcare covers accelerated TMS for depression
event.proposition: UnitedHealthcare adopts a medical policy that covers an accelerated TMS protocol (more than one TMS session per day) for depression in human patients.
event.criterion: TRUE on the effective date of a UnitedHealthcare medical policy or coverage determination guideline, published in UnitedHealthcare's provider policy library, that lists an accelerated TMS protocol (more than one TMS session per day, including accelerated iTBS or fMRI-guided SAINT-type protocols) as proven or medically necessary for major depressive disorder. A policy that covers only standard once-daily TMS, an individual case exception, coverage limited to a clinical trial, or a policy of another payer does not count.

resolution_source.name: UnitedHealthcare medical policies and coverage determination guidelines (UHCprovider.com policy library)

readings: 'United' = UnitedHealthcare, the insurance arm of UnitedHealth Group named in the post title.
'Budging' = changing the coverage stance. Per the forecaster, the stance on the statement date is non-coverage of accelerated TMS for humans, so the positive event is adoption of coverage.
'Accelerated TMS' = protocols with more than one TMS session per day (accelerated iTBS, including fMRI-guided SAINT-type protocols).
'When it comes to humans' = human patients; veterinary coverage is not part of the event.

records.stage_note: On the statement date, per the forecaster, UnitedHealthcare does not cover accelerated TMS for human patients 'despite ample evidence', and the post reports no pending UnitedHealthcare policy change. No class in base-rates.json covers a commercial payer coverage decision, so b is null.
records.note: Denial of a payer coverage change. 'Ain't budging' = will not change its stance: bin A with asserts false, so p(E) = 0.1. 'Any time soon' is not a deadline (anchors.json: 'soon'), so the item is undated (24-month window from 2025-08-09). UnitedHealthcare, a third party, decides. The forecaster holds no disclosed role there, so affiliated is false; his clinic Radial offers accelerated TMS and would gain from coverage, but Radial is not an entity in the event (same reading as owen-0150). Not KNOWN: the present non-coverage is public, the future change is not determined. Sincere: the author invites United to prove him wrong.

Recurring Radial footer: the author's own clinic (Radial, where he is Chief Medical Officer) will 'soon' offer eCOT-AS, a device of Neurolief, where the author is an executive. A launch by the forecaster's own organizations. 'Soon' is also not a deadline.

'Absent a much larger data set, we would see a difference' names no trial, sponsor, sample-size threshold or date. 'A much larger data set' has no benchmark, so any future mortality finding could be read either way. A statistical-power observation about the self-harm intervention literature, not a writable trial_result event.

'We could do these psychotherapeutic things in hospitals, and they might be effective' is a hedged possibility with no named intervention, trial, endpoint, adopting body or date. No practice_adoption or trial_result event can be written.

'They may not want to pay for care that doesn't work' describes a present disposition of insurers in general, and 'I think that's a good idea' is a statement of preference. No payer, policy, code or future date is asserted. A future-tense reading would still fail as VAGUE (no payer, no policy).

Compound conditional on 'if these drugs work on their own', which is itself not a written event (no trial, sponsor or endpoint). Each consequent fails on its own: 'many more people will be able to access them' is a quantifier with no countable set or series; 'drive costs down dramatically' is a comparative with no benchmark or series; 'reduce the need for ... training' has no metric. Not split: no leg is admissible.

'This problem won't solve itself overnight' is a truism about therapist-workforce diversity: 'solve' has no threshold or series and 'overnight' is not a date. The topic also lies outside the five areas.

'A more scalable, accessible, and just treatment for many people' is three comparatives with no benchmark, series or countable set, conditional on an unwritten premise (psilocybin works without adjunctive therapy). Restates owen-1840.

'No one loses out ... other than those in the business of selling unvalidated training' argues about who is harmed if therapy adds nothing. 'Loses out' is not an observable event, no vendor, revenue series or threshold is named, and the premise is unwritten. 'I would argue' is argumentative, not predictive.
Same recurring Radial footer as owen-1836, in a different post (not a DUPLICATE, which needs the same post). Own-organization launch (Radial, Neurolief); 'soon' is not a deadline.

Rules of thumb about which posts perform well on LinkedIn. Social-media engagement is not one of the five areas; 'do well' also has no benchmark. Same reading as the earlier LinkedIn heuristics (owen-0393).
A future debate among readers about the construct validity of an engagement metric is not a regulatory, trial, company, payer or practice outcome.
A training flaw in large language models being 'overcomeable' is outside the five areas; no actor, model, benchmark or date is named. Same reading as the earlier version of this claim (owen-0656).
A mechanism hypothesis about LinkedIn engagement per impression. Social-media metrics are outside the five areas, and 'I would imagine' states a hypothesis with no series or threshold.

Publication of the author's own book ('Don't Panic') is an own-venture publication: a publisher would buy it, but the author controls whether it is pitched, self-published or shelved (same reading as owen-0234). 'Any time soon' is also not a deadline, and book publishing is outside the five areas.
'I'll get out another book soon' is the author's own publishing plan, with no title, publisher or date. Own publication; 'soon' is not a deadline.

Promotional pitch claim: 'this will change once people read this book' names no observable event, measure or series for public access to mentalizing tools. The condition (people read the author's own book, unsold at the statement date) is also under the forecaster's control.
Promotional reader-outcome claim from the pitch ('you won't be so worried'). No measurable outcome, population, instrument or date; the book was not sold.
Promotional pitch claim ('a much quicker journey for you'): a comparative with no benchmark, measure or date.

'You're probably not gonna return it' concerns returns of a book that was not sold; no buyer set, return-rate series, threshold or date. Joke framing around a $30 price; even read sincerely, no company_event or quantity_threshold can be written.
Market-sizing claim from the pitch ('two large audiences'): no sales threshold, series or date for the author's own unsold book. 'Foresee' attaches to audience segments, not to a measurable outcome.
'Has the potential to attain a global audience in subsequent translations' is a possibility with no translation count, market, series or date for an unsold own book.
'Likely the most humorous book ... with limited direct competitors' is a competitive-position comparative with no benchmark, defined set of competitors or measure. Promotional pitch text.
Promotional reader-reaction claim ('they'll appreciate honest guidance') with no measurable outcome, population or date.

The forward leg, 'it will transform the reader's life', is a promotional slogan with no measurable outcome; the other legs are past claims about the author and his patients. Pitch text for an unsold book.
Promotional slogan ('will transform your relationships') with no measurable outcome, population or date.
Conditional promotional slogan ('you'll be able to resolve conflicts of all varieties') with no measurable outcome; 'all varieties' is a quantifier with no countable set.
Promotional slogan ('will totally transform your life'); restates owen-1864. No measurable outcome.

Conditional on the author's own performance ('if I do a really good job'), with a promotional consequent ('you'll learn how to build trust') that has no measurable outcome. The antecedent is under the forecaster's control.
Advice plus a promised effect ('it will save you from some very difficult conversations'). No population, measure, series or date; a technique's benefit to readers is not a writable event.

Sponsor blurb: the author's own clinic (Radial) will 'soon' offer eCOT-AS, a Neurolief device (the author is an executive at Neurolief). Own-organization launch; 'soon' is not a deadline. Same blurb as owen-1836 and owen-1844, in a different post.
Same Radial sponsor blurb (eCOT-AS by Neurolief 'soon') in another post. Own-organization launch; 'soon' is not a deadline.

A generic clinical prognosis for adolescents after a suicide attempt ('the most likely outcome ... is that the kids will be ok'), restating the Bommersbach et al. follow-up data. Not a regulatory, trial, company, payer or practice outcome, and no third party decides it. Same reading as earlier clinical prognoses (owen-0832, owen-0957).

'Functional unblinding will be THE issue on which these compounds and their administration protocols are judged' names no deciding body's observable act, no compound, application or date. 'THE issue' has no test; an FDA decision citing unblinding would need an invented criterion. 'We have learned' also frames it as a lesson already drawn.

'Psilocybin may offer hope' is a present hedged assessment of published data, and 'I look forward to the phase III trial' states anticipation, a wish, as with the earlier 'I look forward to' items (owen-0709, owen-0821, owen-1019). No sponsor, trial or probability word is given for a trial-start event, so the phase III leg is not coded as a forecast.
Promotional 'Get Healthcare At Radial' section: the author's own clinic will 'soon' offer eCOT-AS by Neurolief (the author is an executive there). Own-organization launch; 'soon' is not a deadline.
'So much more is coming' promises educational content from Radial, the author's own clinic. Own content plan; 'coming' is not a deadline.
Teaser for later footnotes in the author's own newsletter series ('more on those to follow'). Own content plan; 'to follow' is not a deadline.

A generic clinical prognosis ('once you have an autoimmune disorder, you will likely have others') restating a clinical generalization. Not one of the five areas, and no third party decides it. Same reading as earlier clinical prognoses.
